title: Pasting hands you the pointer with the new layer picked
goal: Paste something and you are left holding whatever tool you had, with the marquee still live, so the obvious next move, dragging the thing you just pasted, does not work until you switch tools yourself. A paste should leave you with the pointer in hand and the pasted layer picked, ready to move.
notes: Reported by the user on 2026-09-07. Confirmed by reading Sources/Photonz/EditorState+Clipboard.swift: nothing in the paste path calls setTool, so the tool in hand survives the paste. The rule already exists elsewhere and can be copied rather than invented: beginGridAdjustment (EditorState.swift line 309) does exactly this, switching to select when it needs the pointer, and the crop paths do the same at EditorState+Crop.swift lines 57 and 63. Check what the paste already does about picking the layer, since recordPaste (line 165) tracks the ladder of pasted frames for stacking but the picking may be happening elsewhere or not at all. The undo point is worth care: the tool is not part of the document, so restoring it on undo needs deciding rather than assuming, and the audit should say what was chosen.
acceptance: After a paste, the pointer is the tool in hand and the pasted layer is picked, so dragging it moves it straight away
This holds for pasting a layer copied inside the app, a picture from another app, and a copied region
The marquee that was live before the paste is cleared, since the paste is now the thing you are working on
Undo puts back both the document and the tool you were using, so a paste and an undo leave no surprise
Pasting several times in a row still stacks them the way it does now, each one picked in turn
Audit written under queue/audits/ with a paste followed immediately by a drag, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Adversarial review before building. The mock-free part of this is the undo half: the tool is not in the document, so undo cannot restore it by itself, and a tool arriving back several presses after the paste it belonged to would be its own surprise. Bounded it: the tool comes back only when undo is the very next thing you do, only when the pointer is still what is in hand, and never for crop, which is a mode with a half-drawn rectangle the paste already threw away. Also cut the wider version: drops keep whatever tool you had, since a drop already lands where you chose to put it. Filed as a follow-up instead.

Built. New pure type PasteToolReturn in PhotonzCore (Clipboard.swift) holds the tool a run of pastes displaced and answers when to give it back; 14 tests in Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/PasteToolReturnTests.swift written first. App side: paste() captures the tool on the way in, pasteLayer/pasteImage now return the layer they landed, and handOverPointer() switches to select, picks the paste and arms the memory. setTool and perform both clear the memory, so a tool picked by hand or any other edit ends it; undo() and redo() read it. Gated on the new next-only flag next-paste-hands-you-the-pointer, on by default in next, so Current is untouched. Nothing in Releases/ is forked, so no porting needed.

Verified on the running probe app with Scripts/playtest/paste-hands-you-the-pointer-walk.json. Rectangle in hand, paste, tool reads select and the copy is picked; the drag that follows moves it 316,266 -> 650,520 with the layer count unchanged, so it moved rather than drew. Second paste steps to 332,282, still picked. Undo returns the rectangle tool, redo takes the pointer back. A copied region does the same and clears the marquee (region 320,270 240x150 -> none). A plain picture with no Photonz payload, the way one from another app arrives, does the same and its undo hands the measure tool back. Full suite: 4489 tests pass. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-07-paste-hands-you-the-pointer.json with three real window captures.

Rough, recorded in the audit: the tool bar changes shape as the colour swatches leave with the drawing tool; the marquee does not come back on undo (selection has never been in undo history); dropping a file still leaves your tool alone, filed as dropping-a-picture-on-the-canvas-hands-you-the-p.

A paste hands you the pointer with the pasted layer picked, so the drag that follows moves it. Undo hands your tool back, redo takes the pointer again. New pure PasteToolReturn in PhotonzCore with 14 tests, wired through EditorState paste/undo/redo behind the next-only flag next-paste-hands-you-the-pointer. Verified on the probe app with Scripts/playtest/paste-hands-you-the-pointer-walk.json (layer copy, copied region, and a plain picture from outside all covered) and the full 4489-test suite. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-07-paste-hands-you-the-pointer.json. Follow-up filed for drops. Pushed as 2b43882f.
